validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE checked and confirmed. Two independent, contemporaneous Egyptian outlets corroborate this as a real, distinct asset: (1) mubasher.info, 23 Apr 2019, quoting an EGPC/Petroleum Pipelines Co. official ('حافظ'), which lists a slate of Upper-Egypt butagas pipeline projects and states '...جارى الانتهاء من ازدواج خط بوتاجاز "رأس بكر- رأس غارب- أسيوط" بطول 160 كم...' ('duplication of the Ras Bakr-Ras Gharb-Assiut butagas line, 160 km, is nearing completion'); (2) youm7.com, 11 Jan 2020, reporting the Petroleum Minister's inauguration ceremony, quoting Eng. Emad Abdel-Qader (Chairman, Petroleum Pipelines Co.) confirming the duplication ('ازدواج') was executed as two 12-inch parallel segments: Ras Bakr/Ras Gharb (25 km) and Khashm El-Raqaba/New Assiut (130 km), terminating at the 'blowdown room' (غرفة بلوف) of New Assiut. Both sources independently name Petroleum Pipelines Co. (شركة أنابيب البترول) as builder/operator, matching GEM's Operator value exactly (previously MISSING_REF — now filled, see fills). Fuel=LPG (بوتاجاز) and Status=operating are directly supported by context (a ceremonial start-up/'تشغيل' by the Minister) even though 'operating' never appears as a literal token — per standing status-inference rule. PipelineType=transmission is consistent with GEM's treatment of the other bulk LPG lines in this roster (P7333, P7338, P7339) — this is bulk product transport between a coastal receiving point and a bulk blowdown/distribution facility, not a local distribution network. DUPLICATE CHECK vs P7363 'Ras Ghareb-Asyut LPG Pipeline' (305 km): NOT a duplicate. The same mubasher article separately and explicitly states the ORIGINAL single line was already complete before this project: '...تم الانتهاء من تنفيذ خط بوتاجاز "رأس غارب - أسيوط" بطول 305 كم...' (completed Ras Gharb-Assiut butagas line, 305 km) — that is P7363, an exact match on name and length. P7364 is the SEPARATE later duplication/twinning ('ازدواج') project laid parallel to part of that corridor plus a westward extension to Ras Bakr, matching SUMED's own well-documented pattern of twin/parallel product lines. These are two real, distinct physical pipelines, not a double-count. CAVEAT — route is NOT contiguous as the name implies: the youm7 quote is explicit that the 2020 inauguration covered only two segments (25 km + 130 km = 155 km) with a gap in between (Ras Gharb to Khashm El-Raqaba, ~130 km) whose OWN duplication the 2019 mubasher article lists separately as merely PLANNED ('التخطيط لتنفيذ ازدواج خط بوتاجاز "رأس غارب - خشم الرقبة" بطول 130 كم') — i.e. not yet built as of the 2020 inauguration. So 'Ras Bakr-Ras Gharb-Asyut' as a single named line is actually (at least as of 2020) two disconnected parallel-pipe segments riding alongside the pre-existing single P7363 corridor for the un-duplicated middle stretch. This is a plausible, defensible way to model it as one GEM row (it is one investment project under one name), but the route geometry (if ever drawn) needs to reflect two disjoint segments, not one continuous 160 km line. Flagging for route-creation awareness, not as a data-value concern.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile LengthKnown: the two sourced figures disagree (160 vs 155 km). Consider whether GEM's 160 should be revised to the more precise, later, itemized as-built figure of 155 km (25+130), or documented as a range/estimate.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM LengthKnown = 160.00 km, currently cited to mubasher.info (Apr 2019), which does state '...بطول 160 كم' for this project — so the existing ref genuinely supports the value, this is not a fabricated/misapplied citation. BUT it is a forward-looking, PRE-COMPLETION planning statement made ~9 months before the line was actually finished. The later, more authoritative source — youm7.com's Jan 2020 inauguration report, quoting the Petroleum Pipelines Co. chairman on the as-built result — gives an itemized total of 155 km: 'ازدواج القطاع الأول (رأس بكر/رأس غارب)... بطول 25 كيلو متر' + 'القطاع الثانى (خشم الرقبة/أسيوط الجديدة)... بطول 130 كيلو متر' = 25+130 = 155 km, and the same article's lede independently states the inaugurated line's length as 'بطول 155 كيلو متر'. So two independent sources exist, but they DISAGREE (160 vs 155, ~3%), and the more precise, completion-stage, itemized figure is 155 — not 160. This does not rise to a material/order-of-magnitude problem, but under the corroboration rule this is not a clean 'two independent sources agree' case — it is a genuine, if small, conflict. Recommend Update review whether 155 km (itemized, as-built) should replace 160 km (a pre-completion round-number estimate).

validity.researcher_notes: Re-verified the THREE weakest existing citations on this row by fetching them directly (not just trusting a prior 200 status) and testing each against a nonsense sibling slug: (1) Diameter [ref] = hotinformationonline.com/2020/01/11/... — fetched: the rendered page is a 149-character empty WordPress shell ('جريدة المناقصات في مصر ... Designed by Elegant Themes | Powered by WordPress') with ZERO article text. A nonsense sibling slug on the same host returns byte-for-byte the same 149-character shell. This is a confirmed SOFT 404 — the site serves an empty theme page for any URL, live or not — so this citation supports nothing and should not be relied on, even though it 200s. (2) Cost [ref]/Capacity [ref] = enterprise.press/ar/stories/2020/01/12/... — fetched: 461,002 bytes, but the extracted text is pure site chrome/navigation (title tag is the generic 'EnterpriseAM Egypt', no article body, no Arabic pipeline text at all). A nonsense sibling slug returns an IDENTICAL 461,002-byte page. Confirmed SOFT 404 — this old story permalink no longer resolves to real content on this host, it just falls through to a homepage-shell template. url_verifier's earlier PASS on 'Capacity [ref]' for this same URL was therefore a false positive (likely a stale generic token match); a fresh check for '1,600' against the live page FAILS, consistent with there being no article there at all. GOOD NEWS for two of the three values: Diameter (12 in) and Cost (450,000,000 EGP) are BOTH independently and verifiably stated in the youm7.com article already used elsewhere on this row — '...بتنفيذ خط موازى قطر 12 بوصة...' (twice, once per segment) and '...بتكلفة استثمارية 450 مليون جنيه...' (450 million EGP — note a DIFFERENT nearby project in the same article, the Assiut octane-benzene refinery unit, is separately costed at '450 مليون دولار' [$450m] — do not conflate the two). Recommend re-pointing Diameter [ref] and Cost [ref] to youm7.com. BAD NEWS for Capacity: 1,600 Tn/d has no live source at all right now. The two sources in hand describe system-level throughput increases that do not equal 1,600 (mubasher: overall south-Upper-Egypt system planned to rise from 2,600 to 6,000 t/d across multiple projects; youm7: this specific duplication raised throughput from 2,600 to 4,000 t/d, i.e. +1,400 t/d, not 1,600). 1,600 t/d could plausibly be the new parallel line's own nominal/design capacity (as opposed to the measured system throughput delta), which would not contradict either figure, but I could not find any source stating '1,600' directly (WebSearch quota was exhausted this session after one query). Recommend a follow-up ref-only search for Capacity rather than treating the current sourcing as sound.
